overview: This file traces the Allied assessment and revival of Japan’s textile industry after World War II. It combines surveys of mill capacity, wartime damage, industry controls, and raw material needs with detailed cotton, rayon, wool, and silk statistics. Correspondence and reports document the international Textile Mission, occupation policy, export allocations, silk marketing disputes, and negotiations to sell Japanese textiles abroad, especially to Siam.
interest: Detailed industry statistics sit alongside mission records and policy disputes, revealing how occupation officials rebuilt production and negotiated exports.
